title: TS SDK: Tagged-union factory generator + Zod decorator for streaming-parse ergonomics
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Current TS SDK type generation produces Zod schemas and TypeScript types but is awkward when consuming streaming responses that emit partial JSON shapes (common with structured output). Discriminated unions are valid at compile-time, but runtime parsing during streaming requires incremental validation and error-recovery strategies. We also need a lightweight decorator API so callers can annotate handlers with parsing hints (eg. preferred discriminator key, stable schema id) that survive minification and tree-shaking.

Goal: Provide a robust "tagged-union factory" generator that emits: 1) TS types, 2) Zod runtime validators, 3) JSON Schema artifacts, and 4) small decorator helpers that attach metadata to parsers/handlers. This should improve developer ergonomics for structured output and streaming parsing while keeping bundle size low.

Proposed approach:
- Add a generator pass (tsdk-gen-tagged) that takes a model output contract (simple DSL or existing tsdk schema input) and emits:
  - TypeScript discriminated union types with explicit discriminator key/type
  - Zod union validator using .discriminatedUnion when possible, or fallback to refinement-based guards for streaming partials
  - JSON Schema file (compact) with $id for use by server-side eval pipelines
  - A tiny runtime factory: createTaggedParser(schemaId, zodSchema, {discriminatorKey}) -> { parseChunk, finalize }
- Streaming ergonomics:
  - parseChunk(buffer) attempts incremental parse of buffered characters; when a complete object is available, run zod.partial() or pre-compiled incremental validator and emit typed value
  - finalize() flushes remaining buffer and returns remaining parse errors
  - Provide a recoverToNextRoot() helper to skip until next top-level object in noisy streams (common when model emits extra text)
- Decorator helpers:
  - export function AttachSchema(id: string, opts?: {discriminator?: string}) => (fn) attaches non-enumerable metadata on function for runtime ops (metadata should be preserved across bundlers by using static string constants)
  - A small reflectMetadata(fn) utility used by console runtime and CLI runners to auto-wire parsers
- Bundle & perf constraints:
  - Keep runtime helpers <1.5kB gzipped
  - Prefer Zod native methods; only fallback to hand-rolled validators when necessary to support streaming partials
- Testing & compatibility:
  - Add unit tests for full JSON, chopped JSON, interleaved text, and common edge cases
  - Benchmarked parse latency and memory for 1k/10k messages

Acceptance criteria:
- Generator creates TS types, Zod schema, and JSON Schema for a sample contract (see examples below)
- Runtime parser supports chunked input with at least 90% success recovery on typical LLM noise patterns (extra punctuation/text between objects)
- Decorator helper metadata accessible from Console integration to auto-bind handlers
- Bundle increase measured and kept under 1.5kB gzipped for runtime helpers
- Documentation example added to SDK README (code sample + streaming consumer pattern)

Example contract (input to generator):
- contract: "ChatAction"
- discriminator: "action_type"
- variants: [
  { name: "reply", props: { text: "string", confidence: "number?" } },
  { name: "search", props: { query: "string", results: "array" } },
  { name: "noop", props: {} }
]

Example output (sketch):
- TypeScript:
  type ChatAction = { action_type: "reply"; text: string; confidence?: number } | { action_type: "search"; query: string; results: unknown[] } | { action_type: "noop" }
- Zod:
  const Reply = z.object({ action_type: z.literal("reply"), text: z.string(), confidence: z.number().optional() })
  const ChatAction = z.discriminatedUnion("action_type", [Reply, Search, Noop])
- Runtime factory usage (consumer):
  const parser = createTaggedParser('ChatAction.v1', ChatAction, { discriminatorKey: 'action_type' })
  stream.on('data', chunk => { const items = parser.parseChunk(chunk); items.forEach(handle) })
  await parser.finalize()

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should the generator prefer z.object().passthrough() vs. strict() for future-proofing model extra fields? Proposal: default passthrough, provide CLI flag --strict
- How to ensure metadata survives minifiers? We plan to keep schema ids as exported const strings and require attachSchema(const) usage; investigate Terser caveats in prod builds
- Edge-case performance: large arrays inside objects may require streaming-aware validators; start with partial object parsing and extend if we see regressions
